newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's 3-yr bond yields close edge lower.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's 3-yr bond yields close edge lower.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporate bonds closed slightly lower on Wednesday on the back of strong demand for blue-chip issues, brokers said.
Three-month CD yields rose as expectations of a further rise dampened sentiment, they said.
The overnight call rate fell on increased offerings by insurance companies, they said.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.44 pct vs Tuesday's 12.45
* 3-mth CDs close at 12.50 pct vs Tuesday's 12.45
* Average overnight call rate at 12.10 pct vs Tuesday's 12.21
Brokers said the three-year yields would move in a narrow range around the 12.45 percent level for the rest of this week, although new issues are expected to rise on Thursday.
They estimated new corporate bond issues at 220 billion won on Thursday, up from 75 billion today.
Three-month CD yields closed higher on expectations that yields would further rise.
Yields on commercial papers with the same maturity with CDs remained relatively high, brokers said.
